title: HomeGuard Homeowners Policy — Reversal of Mold Remediation Seepage Denials
content:
**Claims desk page — HomeGuard Homeowners Policy, fungi, wet rot and bacteria remediation**

## Where this applies

This policy re-settles the fungi, wet rot and bacteria remediation of the most recently reported claim on a HomeGuard Homeowners Policy when the claim's first notice records a freeze or a sudden and accidental discharge of water while the mold remediation stands on the claim only as a repeated-seepage denial entry, and it fixes the mold payment that replaces that denial.

Read as a condition on the claim file:

| What the claim file shows | Within this policy |
|---|---|
| Most recent first-notice entry records a freeze or a sudden and accidental discharge of water, and the mold remediation stands only as a repeated-seepage denial entry | Yes — the mold remediation is re-settled and a mold payment replaces the denial |

The claim concerned is the one of the most recent first-notice entry on the policy.

## What the payment records

- The payment is a new **payment entry on the mold coverage part** of the claim, replacing the repeated-seepage denial entry of the mold remediation and carrying that denial's replacement-cost value.
- **Kind of payment:** full replacement cost when the mold replacement-cost value is at or below the package's no-holdback threshold, and actual-cash-value initial otherwise.
- **Nothing is withheld** on a mold payment and **no deductible is recorded** on it.
- **Payee:** the payment is payable to the insured alone, because the mortgagee co-payee rule reaches only dwelling and other-structures payments.

## Tool: `settle_denied_mold_remediation_0cacd0ff`

**Capability.** Issues the mold (fungi, wet rot and bacteria) remediation payment that replaces a repeated-seepage denial of the mold remediation on a HomeGuard homeowners claim. One call records one new payment on the mold coverage part of the named claim, carrying the replacement-cost value of the denial it replaces, the amount paid and the payee; nothing is withheld and no deductible is recorded on it. The claim's paid total rises by the amount, and the insured sees a new mold payment on the claim file dated today.

**How it is invoked.** This is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `settle_denied_mold_remediation_0cacd0ff` and then calls it.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `home_policy_id` | Reference number of the HomeGuard policy the claim is made under, as returned by the home policy lookup for the verified customer | Id |
| `claim_number` | The claim number exactly as it appears on the claim's first-notice entry returned by the claim lookup | Verbatim, copied character for character |
| `source_entry_id` | Reference number of the repeated-seepage denial entry of the mold remediation that this payment replaces, as returned by the claim lookup | Id |
| `payment_type` | The kind of mold payment | Enum: `replacement_cost_full` when the remediation value is at or below the policy's no-holdback amount; `acv_initial` when it is above it (remediation carries no depreciation, so nothing is ever withheld) |
| `amount` | Amount paid on the mold remediation | USD, 2 decimal places, positive |
| `payee` | Who the payment is made out to | Enum: `insured` when the check is payable to the named insured alone; `insured_and_mortgagee` when the mortgagee on file is named as co-payee with the insured |

**Return.** On success the tool returns, as text: status `recorded`; `payment_entry_id`, the reference number of the new mold payment entry; `claim_number`, the claim paid; `payment_type`, the kind recorded; `amount`, the USD amount paid to 2 decimal places; `payee`, who the payment is made out to; and `entry_date`, the date of the payment in YYYY-MM-DD form.

## Illustration of a call (hypothetical values)

A hypothetical call with `home_policy_id` "HP-0000", `claim_number` "HC-0000-01", `source_entry_id` "DEN-0000", `payment_type` `replacement_cost_full`, `amount` 1234.56 and `payee` `insured` returns status `recorded` with a new `payment_entry_id` and the day's `entry_date`. The values shown are placeholders, not policy figures.
